history.summary: CSV town corrected: the temple is on Yellammagudda hill (Yellammanna Gudda), ~5 km from Saundatti town in Belagavi district, not in Belgaum city. Dedicated to Renuka Devi, worshipped as Yellamma ('Mother of All') - wife of sage Jamadagni and mother of Parashurama - it is one of South India's major Shakti pilgrimage sites, drawing millions during the Yellamma Jatre, one of Karnataka's largest fairs. Wikipedia notes the hilltop was earlier called Siddhachal Parvat, lies in the Sidhachal/Ramagiri range overlooking the Malaprabha river, and shows archaeological occupation from the 8th-11th centuries plus earlier megalithic tombs. The complex includes shrines of Ganesha, Mallikarjuna, Parashurama, Eknath and Siddheshwara, plus the Deepa Stambhas and three sacred tanks (Kumkum, Yoni and Arihan Kundam). The temple is associated with the historic Devadasi dedication practice, eradicated in Karnataka by the 1982 Devadasi Prohibition Act. The government manages the temple; coordinates are from Wikipedia (15.754, 75.16).

name: Saundatti Yellamma Temple
town_description: Saundatti (Savadatti) is an ancient town in Belagavi district, Karnataka, once the first capital of the Ratta dynasty. It is best known as the gateway to the Renuka Yellamma Temple on Yellammagudda hill about 5 km away, which draws millions of pilgrims. The town has an 18th-century fort built by the Sirasangi Desai with eight bastions, and sits near the Malaprabha river, whose Naviluteertha Dam forms the Renuka Sagara reservoir named after the goddess.

travel.road: Yellammagudda is ~5 km from Saundatti town by road; motorable road reaches the hilltop temple, and pilgrims also climb on foot
